# S&P Global U.S. Forecast Update August 2026 

Aug. 11, 2026

By Niaoniao You, EBRC Senior Economic Forecaster

Consumer spending resilience hints at improved near-term outlook

Image

 

S&P Global have released their August 2026 forecast update for the U.S. economy. The near-term forecast was revised up due to stronger-than-expected growth in the second quarter of 2026 and improved outlooks for consumer spending in the third quarter. However, this momentum hinges on the development of conflicts in the Middle East, performance of equity markets, and employment and GDP data revisions. 

Real GDP growth is forecast to stay at 2.1% in 2026 before picking up to 2.3% in 2027, compared to 2.8% in 2024 and 2.1% in 2025. On a quarterly basis, the forecast calls for real GDP to increase through 2036 (no recession).

# Q3 GDP Nowcast Slips to 3.58% as the Model Digests July Inflation and Jobs Data

 Date: 2026-08-12 Author: GDP Dynamics Share 

The GDP Dynamics nowcast for third-quarter U.S. real GDP growth fell to 3.58% SAAR on August 12, down 0.23 percentage point from the August 7 estimate. That works out to roughly 0.90% growth quarter over quarter.

The decline looks modest, but there was considerably more movement underneath the headline number. Consumer spending, net exports, business fixed investment, inventories and government all made positive moves in the model, while residential investment weakened. The net result was still a slightly lower overall estimate.

# US retail sales extend growth streak to 10 months

US retail sales continued to grow in July, extending a 10-month run of increases, but the pace of annual growth slowed sharply from June.

 Mohamed Dabo August 12, 2026 

Consumer demand remained uneven, with electronics and digital products outperforming while building supplies and sporting goods declined. / Credit: Achmad_Khoeron via Shutterstock

US retail sales increased for a 10th consecutive month in July 2026, although annual growth slowed sharply from June, according to the latest CNBC/NRF Retail Monitor.

Total retail sales, excluding car dealers and petrol stations, rose 0.32% on a seasonally adjusted month-on-month basis and were 5.15% higher than in July 2025.

# US services activity stays strong in July, input costs rise

 By Thomson Reuters Aug 5, 2026 | 7:31 AM 

By Lucia Mutikani

WASHINGTON, Aug 5 (Reuters) – The U.S. services sector maintained a strong pace of growth in July, but strong demand is colliding with supply constraints, driving up input costs for businesses and potentially keeping inflation elevated for a while.

The survey from the Institute for Supply Management on Wednesday added to manufacturing data this week in suggesting that the economy started the third quarter on a solid note, despite headwinds from the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, now in its sixth month. ​Most economists viewed the data as supportive of expectations that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates this year.
